questions.stem:
For the exothermic reaction:
$$\mathrm{N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)}$$
Which of the following conditions will shift the equilibrium in the forward direction?

options.label: A
options.content: Increasing the temperature and increasing the pressure

options.label: B
options.content: Decreasing the temperature and increasing the pressure

options.label: C
options.content: Decreasing the temperature and decreasing the pressure

options.label: D
options.content: Increasing the temperature and decreasing the pressure

questions.solution:
For the forward reaction:
1. It is exothermic ($\Delta H < 0$), so decreasing the temperature shifts the equilibrium in the forward direction.
2. $\Delta n_g = 2 - 4 = -2 < 0$, so increasing the pressure (decreasing volume) shifts the equilibrium towards the side with fewer moles of gas (forward direction).

questions.stem:
For the reaction:
$$\mathrm{PCl_5(g) \rightleftharpoons PCl_3(g) + Cl_2(g)},\quad \Delta H > 0$$
Which of the following conditions will shift the equilibrium in the forward direction?

options.label: D
options.content: Decreasing the volume of the container

questions.solution: The reaction is endothermic ($\Delta H > 0$). According to Le Chatelier's principle, increasing the temperature shifts the equilibrium of an endothermic reaction in the forward direction. Increasing pressure/decreasing volume shifts it towards fewer moles (backward), and adding $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ shifts it backward.

questions.stem: For the reaction $\mathrm{A(g)} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{B(g)}$, the value of equilibrium constant is $100$ at $300\ \mathrm{K}$. If the initial concentration of $\mathrm{A(g)}$ is $1\ \mathrm{M}$, the concentration of $\mathrm{B(g)}$ at equilibrium is $x \times 10^{-2}\ \mathrm{M}$. The value of $x$ is ___________. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
Let equilibrium concentration of $\mathrm{B}$ be $y\ \mathrm{M}$.
At equilibrium, $[\mathrm{A}] = 1 - y$ and $[\mathrm{B}] = y$.
$K_c = \frac{[\mathrm{B}]}{[\mathrm{A}]} = \frac{y}{1-y} = 100 \implies y = 100 - 100y \implies 101y = 100 \implies y = \frac{100}{101} \approx 0.99\ \mathrm{M}$.
$y = 99 \times 10^{-2}\ \mathrm{M}$. Thus, $x = 99$.

questions.stem:
For the reaction:
$$\mathrm{PCl}_5(g) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{PCl}_3(g) + \mathrm{Cl}_2(g)$$
the forward reaction is favoured by:

options.label: A
options.content: introducing an inert gas at constant volume

options.label: B
options.content: introducing chlorine gas at constant volume

options.label: C
options.content: introducing an inert gas at constant pressure

options.label: D
options.content: increasing the pressure of the system

questions.solution:
The reaction shows an increase in the number of moles of gas ($\Delta n_g = 2 - 1 = 1 > 0$).
- Adding inert gas at constant pressure increases the volume, shifting the equilibrium to the side with more moles of gas (forward direction).
- Inert gas at constant volume has no effect.
- Increasing pressure shifts it to the left (less moles).
- Adding product $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ shifts it to the left.

questions.stem: For the reaction $2\mathrm{NO_2(g)} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N_2O_4(g)}$, the value of $\Delta H$ is negative (exothermic). The yield of $\mathrm{N_2O_4}$ at equilibrium can be increased by:
questions.solution: For $2\mathrm{NO_2(g)} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N_2O_4(g)}$, $\Delta n_g = 1 - 2 = -1 < 0$. High pressure shifts equilibrium forward (towards fewer moles of gas). Since $\Delta H < 0$, low temperature shifts equilibrium forward (Le Chatelier's Principle). Thus, decreasing temperature and increasing pressure increases the yield.

questions.stem:
For the reaction $A(g) \rightleftharpoons B(g)$, the value of the equilibrium constant at $298\ \mathrm{K}$ is $100$. If the value of standard Gibbs free energy change of the reaction ($\Delta G^{\circ}$) at $298\ \mathrm{K}$ is $-x \times 10^2\ \mathrm{J\ mol^{-1}}$, the value of $x$ is _________ (Nearest integer).
(Given: $R = 8.314\ \mathrm{J\ K^{-1}\ mol^{-1}}$, $\ln 10 = 2.3$)
questions.solution:
$\Delta G^{\circ} = -RT \ln K = -8.314 \times 298 \times \ln(100) = -8.314 \times 298 \times 2 \ln(10)$
$\Delta G^{\circ} = -8.314 \times 298 \times 2 \times 2.3 \approx -11396.8\ \mathrm{J\ mol^{-1}}$
$\Delta G^{\circ} = -113.97 \times 10^2\ \mathrm{J\ mol^{-1}}$.
Thus, $x \approx 114$.

questions.stem:
For the reaction:
$$\mathrm{PCl_5(g) \rightleftharpoons PCl_3(g) + Cl_2(g)}$$
the forward reaction is favored by:

options.label: B
options.content: decreasing the volume of the container

options.label: C
options.content: introducing an inert gas at constant pressure

options.label: D
options.content: introducing an inert gas at constant volume

questions.solution:
Here, $\Delta n_g = 1 + 1 - 1 = 1 > 0$.
According to Le Chatelier's principle:
- Adding inert gas at constant pressure increases the volume, favoring the side with more moles of gas (forward).
- Adding inert gas at constant volume has no effect.
- Increasing pressure or decreasing volume shifts the equilibrium backward.

questions.stem:
For the reaction:
$$\mathrm{N}_2(g) + 3\mathrm{H}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH}_3(g) \quad \Delta H < 0$$
Which of the following conditions will shift the equilibrium to the right?
questions.solution:
According to Le Chatelier's principle:
1) Since the reaction is exothermic ($\Delta H < 0$), decreasing temperature shifts the equilibrium in the forward direction (to the right).
2) The forward reaction occurs with a decrease in the number of gaseous moles (from 4 to 2). Thus, increasing pressure shifts the equilibrium to the side with fewer moles (forward/right).

questions.stem: For the reaction $\text{PCl}_5(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{PCl}_3(g) + \text{Cl}_2(g)$, the forward reaction is favored by :

options.label: A
options.content: increasing the pressure at constant volume

options.label: B
options.content: decreasing the volume at constant temperature

options.label: C
options.content: adding an inert gas at constant pressure

options.label: D
options.content: adding an inert gas at constant volume

questions.solution:
For the given reaction, $\Delta n_g = 1 + 1 - 1 = 1 > 0$.
Adding an inert gas at constant pressure increases the total volume, decreasing the partial pressures of the components. To counteract this, the equilibrium shifts in the direction of more moles (forward direction).

questions.stem: For the reaction $\mathrm{PCl_5(g) \rightleftharpoons PCl_3(g) + Cl_2(g)}$, the forward reaction at constant temperature is favored by:

options.label: A
options.content: Introducing an inert gas at constant volume

options.label: B
options.content: Introducing chlorine gas at constant volume

options.label: C
options.content: Introducing an inert gas at constant pressure

options.label: D
options.content: Increasing the total pressure of the system

questions.solution:
The total number of gaseous moles increases in the forward direction ($\Delta n_g = 1 > 0$).
Adding an inert gas at constant pressure increases the volume, which shifts the equilibrium towards the side with more moles of gas (forward direction).

questions.stem: For the reaction $2\mathrm{NO}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N}_2\mathrm{O}_4(g)$, the value of $\Delta H$ is $-57.2\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$. Under which of the following conditions will the yield of $\mathrm{N}_2\mathrm{O}_4$ be maximum?
questions.solution: The reaction is exothermic ($\Delta H < 0$), so low temperature favors the forward reaction. The reaction has $\Delta n_g = 1 - 2 = -1 < 0$, so high pressure favors the forward reaction. Thus, low temperature and high pressure yield maximum $\mathrm{N}_2\mathrm{O}_4$.

questions.stem:
For the reaction:
$$\text{PCl}_5(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{PCl}_3(g) + \text{Cl}_2(g)$$
the forward reaction is favored by:

options.label: B
options.content: Adding inert gas at constant volume

options.label: C
options.content: Adding inert gas at constant pressure

questions.solution: The dissociation of $\text{PCl}_5$ is endothermic and involves an increase in the number of moles of gas ($\Delta n_g = 1 > 0$). Under constant pressure conditions, adding an inert gas increases the total volume, shifting the equilibrium towards the side with more moles of gas (forward direction).

questions.stem:
For the reaction:
$$\mathrm{PCl}_5(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{PCl}_3(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{g})$$
which of the following conditions will favor the forward reaction according to Le Chatelier's principle?

options.label: A
options.content: Increasing the pressure of the system

options.label: B
options.content: Addition of inert gas at constant volume

options.label: C
options.content: Addition of inert gas at constant pressure

questions.solution:
For the given reaction, $\Delta n_g = 1 + 1 - 1 = +1 > 0$.
Adding an inert gas at constant pressure increases the volume of the system, driving the equilibrium towards the side with more moles of gas (forward direction).

questions.stem: For the reaction $\mathrm{PCl_5(g) \rightleftharpoons PCl_3(g) + Cl_2(g)}$, the forward reaction is favored by:

options.label: D
options.content: Adding an inert gas at constant volume

questions.solution: The dissociation of $\mathrm{PCl_5}$ involves an increase in the number of moles of gas ($\Delta n_g = 1 > 0$). According to Le Chatelier's principle, decreasing the pressure shifts the equilibrium towards the side with more moles of gas (i.e., the forward direction).

questions.stem:
For the following equilibrium reaction:
$$\mathrm{N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)} \quad \Delta H < 0$$
Which of the following conditions will shift the equilibrium in the forward direction?

options.label: C
options.content: Increasing the volume of the container

questions.solution:
According to Le Chatelier's principle:
1. Since the forward reaction is exothermic ($\Delta H < 0$), decreasing the temperature shifts it forward.
2. Increasing the concentration of reactants ($\mathrm{N_2}$ or $\mathrm{H_2}$) shifts the equilibrium to the right (forward direction).
3. Increasing pressure (or decreasing volume) shifts the equilibrium towards the side with fewer gaseous moles (forward).

questions.stem:
For the exothermic reaction:
$$\mathrm{N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)}$$
which of the following conditions will shift the equilibrium to the right (towards product formation)?
questions.solution: Since the forward reaction is exothermic, decreasing the temperature shifts equilibrium to the right. Also, since $\Delta n_g = 2 - 4 = -2 < 0$, increasing the pressure shifts the equilibrium to the side with fewer moles of gas (the right).
